title: A Good Servant of Christ Jesus

verses.text: Now the Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons,
influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected,
because it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.
But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.
For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.
To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.
Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

context.author: Paul the apostle (1:1), though some scholars question this
context.genre: Pastoral letter, personal advice from a mentor
context.audience: Timothy, Paul’s younger coworker, left in Ephesus
context.setting: Paul warns that in later times some will depart from the faith, forbidding marriage and certain foods. He tells Timothy that everything created by God is good and to be received with thanksgiving, and urges Timothy to be an example for believers, to devote himself to Scripture, and to watch his life and teaching closely.
context.custom: Some early ascetic groups forbade marriage and meat as marks of holiness. Paul says this is wrong, as God created food and marriage to be received with thanks. “Let no one despise your youth” (v.12) was said of a man perhaps in his thirties.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 5 explains how to treat different groups in the church.
context.timelineBible: “Everything created by God is good” (v.4) echoes Genesis 1:31. The laying on of hands (v.14) follows the pattern in Numbers 27:18-23 when Moses commissioned Joshua.
context.sparkNotes: In later times some will depart from the faith, forbidding marriage and requiring abstinence from foods. But everything created by God is good, sanctified by the word and prayer. Train yourself for godliness, which holds promise for the present life and the life to come. Let no one despise your youth, but set an example. Devote yourself to public reading, exhortation, and teaching. Keep a close watch on yourself and the teaching.

translation.meaning: A pattern or mold others can follow.

otBackground.note: God saw everything he had made, and it was very good.

overview.summary: False teachers forbid what God made good. Timothy should be an example, devote himself to Scripture, and watch his life and teaching.
overview.settingLine: Paul writes to Timothy, who is working in Ephesus.

history.t: Paul says some will forbid marriage and demand abstaining from foods (4:3). He does not name the group. Suggestions include Jewish food teaching and ascetic movements; some Gnostic groups of the 2nd century did discourage marriage, but that is later than the letter. Scholars cannot say who is meant.

Paul tells Timothy, "Let no one despise your youth" (4:12). Writers of the time used words for "youth" of men well into their thirties. Timothy was already a disciple when Paul first met him (Acts 16:1-3), so he could have been in his thirties when this letter was written, but no source gives his age.

customs.t: Paul tells Timothy to devote himself to "the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching" (4:13). Synagogues read the Law and the Prophets aloud (Luke 4:16-20; Acts 13:15), and Paul expected his letters to be read aloud to churches (Colossians 4:16; 1 Thessalonians 5:27).

Paul reminds Timothy of the gift given "through prophecy with the laying on of hands by the council of elders" (4:14), and 2 Timothy 1:6 says it came through Paul's own hands. In Scripture the laying on of hands marks blessing (Genesis 48:14), setting apart (Numbers 27:18-23; Acts 6:6; 13:3) and healing. The two verses may describe one event or two.

archaeology.t: Scripture was read from scrolls. The Dead Sea Scrolls include the Great Isaiah Scroll, a complete scroll of Isaiah copied about 125-100 BC. In 2 Timothy 4:13 Paul asks for "the scrolls, especially the parchments," so books were among his few possessions.

Paul says "physical training is of some value" (4:8). Ephesus had a stadium and large bath-gymnasium complexes where men exercised. The surviving buildings are mostly Roman and many are later than Paul, but they show how central athletics were to the life of a Greek city.

overview.discussion: Paul says to train for godliness. What daily habit would help me grow spiritually the way exercise helps the body?
overview.book: The first letter to Timothy · 6 chapters. A mentor’s guide to leading a church well.
overview.author: Paul

historicalImage.caption: Still Life with Open Bible, by Vincent van Gogh (1885). First Timothy 4:13 tells Timothy to give his attention to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation and to teaching. The painting is from the Netherlands, long after Paul, but it shows the book at the center of a community's life.
